summary.headline: School Committee approves a $7.1M bond sale for athletic facilities, ratifies two labor agreements, and plans a student cell phone ban.
summary.summary: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee approved the sale of a $7.115 million general obligation bond to finance Algonquin Regional High School's athletic complex and amenities building. The committee ratified collective bargaining agreements with high school custodians and Unit C educational support professionals following an executive session. Officials also detailed upcoming high school policies for fall 2026, including mandatory school-issued Chromebooks ending the Bring Your Own Device model and plans for an app-based cell phone ban during school hours.

topics.title: Recognition of retiring faculty and staff
topics.summary: District administrators honored retiring teachers and staff who contributed a cumulative 175-plus years of service to Northborough and Southborough public schools. Individual recognition was given to applied arts and technology teacher Christine Ferrara, English teacher Deborah Saltsman, and applied arts department chair George Clark.
key_details: Christine Ferrara retired after teaching applied arts and technology from 1998 to 2026.
Deborah Saltsman retired after teaching high school English from 2005 to 2026.
George Clark retired after serving as applied arts teacher and department chair from 1996 to 2026.
Other retiring staff recognized included Mary Beth Pappas, Mr. Allaire, and Mrs. Cronin.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee addressed several procedural items, including approving past open and executive session minutes, reappointing the district treasurer, accepting educational donations, and reviewing monthly personnel transactions.
key_details: Reappointed Joseph Mekelburg as regional school district treasurer.
Accepted donations from Table Talk Pies (five cases of pies), Texas Instruments (three graphing calculators), and NumWorks (swag bags for the math team).
Reviewed monthly personnel reports noting the resignation and hiring of high school mathematics teachers.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved; treasurer reappointed; donations accepted.

topics.title: Athletic complex bond sale approval
topics.summary: The committee voted to award and approve the sale of general obligation school bonds to fund the athletic complex and amenities building construction. Favorable bidding conditions allowed the district to resize the bond issue downward from $7.735 million to $7.115 million while securing a low borrowing rate.
key_details: The winning bid was submitted by Loop Capital Markets LLC among nine competitive bids.
The bond was resized to $7,115,000 with a reoffering premium of $736,790, yielding gross proceeds of $7,851,790.
Final true interest cost was 3.07%, retaining the district's double-A-plus bond rating.
Total debt service over the life of the bond through June 15, 2039, will be $9,551,325 ($2.436 million in total interest).
topics.why_it_matters: Locks in long-term borrowing costs for major regional athletic facility improvements with lower net borrowing than originally projected.

topics.title: Subcommittee and liaison assignments for 2026-2027
topics.summary: The committee filled several liaison and subcommittee vacancies for the upcoming academic year across both towns.
key_details: Appointed representatives to the Audit Subcommittee, Capital Planning Committee, and Student Advisory Committee.
Assigned liaisons to the Technology Working Group and the Southborough Select Board.
Noted continuing vacancies on the Solar Feasibility Study Group and Legislative Ad Hoc Group.
topics.outcome: Assignments established for open subcommittee seats.

topics.title: Staff technology lease agreement
topics.summary: Administrators reported on shifting from purchasing 25 to 30 replacement laptops each year to a four-year lease model for faculty computers. The district negotiated a lease for 110 MacBook laptops covered by AppleCare Plus to refresh educator computers across Algonquin Regional High School within the existing operating budget.
key_details: Covers 110 MacBook laptops for educators, prioritizing staff with aging devices.
Cost is funded within existing operational budget allocations rather than requiring new appropriations.
Includes an option to purchase the devices at the end of the four-year lease term.
topics.outcome: Informational update; lease executed under administrative authority.

topics.title: International student travel liability insurance
topics.summary: Following committee approval of an EF Educational Tours student trip abroad, administration confirmed that while the tour company carries insurance, the district remains liable as the sponsoring body. The district is securing a supplemental insurance rider through the Massachusetts Interlocal Insurance Association (MIIA) to cover students and staff chaperones.
key_details: District workers' compensation applies to travelling staff only for conditions that would apply domestically.
A separate MIIA insurance rider is being finalized to provide comprehensive foreign liability protection.
Over 30 students expressed interest in the overseas trip, prompting a selection lottery.
topics.outcome: Informational update; administration is executing the insurance rider.

topics.title: Food services survey results and cafeteria updates
topics.summary: The committee reviewed results from a May-June student food services survey evaluating meals provided by Whitsons Food Service. While 95 percent of students are aware of universal free meals and 80 percent eat cafeteria lunches daily, students requested larger portion sizes, consistent quality, and expanded dietary options. Committee members also discussed the return of the school's traditional chocolate chip cookie recipe.
key_details: Roughly 80 percent of students eat school lunch daily, favoring items like pizza, nacho bars, and chicken sandwiches.
Student concerns centered on portion sizes, preparation consistency, and the need for more vegetarian and vegan options.
Whitsons will collaborate with high school administrators to develop a formal improvement action plan for the fall.
The high school parent-teacher organization partnered with cafeteria staff to recreate the school's original cookie recipe for senior celebrations.
topics.outcome: Whitsons and administration will present a response plan to the committee in the fall.

topics.title: Ratification of custodian and support staff contracts
topics.summary: After an executive session on collective bargaining, the committee reconvened in open session to formally vote on new labor agreements with regional high school custodians and Algonquin Regional Teachers Association Unit C educational support professionals.
key_details: Ratified contract with Algonquin Regional High School Custodians.
Ratified contract with Algonquin Regional Teachers Association Unit C (Educational Support Professionals).
topics.outcome: Both collective bargaining agreements approved unanimously.
topics.why_it_matters: Establishes multi-year wages, benefits, and working conditions for high school support staff and custodians.

topics.title: 1:1 computing rollout and cell phone restrictions
topics.summary: High school administrators announced that starting in fall 2026, Algonquin Regional High School will transition all grades to school-issued Chromebooks, fully ending the Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) model. Administration also detailed plans to restrict cell phone use during school hours using software management tools, aligning with anticipated state guidance on bell-to-bell distraction-free schools.
key_details: All students in grades 9 through 12 will receive a district Chromebook in fall 2026 to ensure security, uniform software, and equity.
The school is piloting mobile device management software (such as Dorman) that locks student phones in an app during the school day while permitting emergency overrides.
Anticipated state policy calls for bell-to-bell restrictions, prohibiting cell phone use in classrooms and hallways.
Officials will present final cell phone protocol details to the committee in the fall.
topics.outcome: Informational update; final policy implementation scheduled for fall 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: Directly impacts every high school student and family regarding device usage, classroom learning, and cell phone access during the school day.

topics.title: Innovation Career Pathways state initiative
topics.summary: Career Development Coordinator Michelle Kalin presented a proposal to apply for Massachusetts Innovation Career Pathways (ICP) designation in business and finance. The program integrates technical coursework, advanced academic classes, and a 100-hour capstone project or internship to connect classroom instruction with regional workforce demand.
key_details: Requires two technical courses, two advanced courses (AP or concurrent enrollment), and a 100-hour culminating capstone or internship.
The 2026-2027 school year will serve as the planning and grant submission phase, with student enrollment targeting the incoming freshman class for participation starting sophomore year.
Initial cohort target is approximately 20 students, with potential future expansion into clean energy or computer science pathways.
topics.outcome: District will submit the state planning application; committee requested a progress update in spring 2027.

topics.title: FY26 budget transfers and year-end financial review
topics.summary: Administrators presented the monthly general fund expenditure report through May 31, 2026, showing an unencumbered balance of $543,518 (1.83 percent of the operating budget). The committee approved an over-budget transfer of $7,592 from teacher salaries to cover long-term substitutes.
key_details: Year-to-date expenditures reached $24,240,553 with $4,906,123 encumbered, leaving a $543,518 balance.
Approved a $7,591.75 transfer into the long-term substitute line item to cover a staff medical leave exceeding 30 days.
Voted to accept the FY26 Statement of Revenue and June 30, 2025 financial balance sheet.
topics.outcome: Voted to approve line item transfers and accept financial statements.

votes.motion: Approve the sale of general obligation school bonds in the resized amount of $7,115,000 to Loop Capital Markets LLC at a true interest cost of 3.07 percent.
Approve collective bargaining agreements with Algonquin Regional High School Custodians and Algonquin Regional Teachers Association Unit C Educational Support Professionals.
Accept the FY26 monthly General Fund report as of May 31, 2026, and approve the overexpended function code transfer of $7,591.75 from teacher salaries to long-term substitutes.
Approve and accept the FY26 Statement of Revenue as presented.
Accept the district financial data balance sheet as of June 30, 2025.
